items.title: Okuama: When Political Blame Ignores the Constitution, Fuels Blackmail
items.description: By Ufuoma Egbe The tragedy of Okuama has left deep wounds. Families have lost loved ones, a community has suffered devastation, and several Okuama leaders have remained in detention for an agonising period. Their plight deserves justice, compassion and sustained public attention. But precisely because the tragedy is so painful, it must not become an excuse for political blackmail that disregards facts, constitutional boundaries and good conscience. The recent attack on Senator Ede Dafinone over the continued detention of Okuama leaders is a case in point. In his call to reject Dafinone in 2027, by Comrade Ogheneyore Israel Okerevwodjaye, one of Omo-Agege’s Media aides portrays the senator as having remained silent while Okuama suffered. The argument suggests that Dafinone should have ensured the detainees’ release and that his failure to do so amounts to failed representation. That may be politically convenient, but does it survive constitutional and factual scrutiny? A senator is a legislator, not a military commander, judge or prison authority. The Constitution gives the National Assembly legislative, representative and oversight responsibilities; it does not confer on an individual senator the power to order the Nigerian Army to release a detainee, issue judicial orders or personally enforce court judgments. The legitimate question, therefore, is not whether Dafinone personally released anyone, but whether he used the powers available to him to advocate justice, due process and the interests of his Okuama constituents. The public record does not support the claim that Dafinone was silent. Media reports in March 2025 documented his calls for justice for detained Okuama citizens, insisting that they should either be released or tried before a competent court. He also advocated the rehabilitation and rebuilding of Okuama, including homes, schools, healthcare facilities and roads. His engagement did not suddenly begin because the 2027 elections are approaching. His participation in Senate discussions on the Okuama tragedy was recorded as far back as March 2024. Dafinone’s interventions also extended beyond public statements. He was among the early Urhobo stakeholders who visited the Ewu-Okuama Internally Displaced Persons camp, where he donated food items and offered support to displaced residents and their families. In April 2024, he was also involved in engagements surrounding the release of the Ewu monarch, King Clement Ikolo, from military custody. The monarch was released to Dafinone, who signed as surety. That development followed engagements with the military authorities and demonstrated the level of confidence built through those interactions. There was another intervention that should not be ignored. On December 17, 2024, 83-year-old Dennis Okugbaye, who was reportedly critically ill while in military custody in Port Harcourt, was released to Dafinone following his intervention. It is legitimate to ask: were these interventions mere accidents? Or do they demonstrate that the senator was actively engaging the authorities on the welfare of people affected by the Okuama crisis? While sensitive negotiations with security authorities may not always be conducted publicly, their effectiveness should be judged by outcomes, not simply by the volume of media statements. The continued detention of some Okuama leaders, particularly in the face of a reported court order, is certainly deserving of urgent attention. But that responsibility cannot simply be transferred to one senator. In June 2026, the Federal High Court sitting in Warri reportedly ordered the unconditional release of Prof. Arthur Ekpekpo and other detained Okuama leaders. That order belongs to the judiciary, while its enforcement rests with the appropriate executive and security authorities. If a valid court order is not obeyed, the critical questions are: which institution is responsible for enforcing it, why has it not been enforced, and who should answer for that failure? Dafinone is not the Nigerian Army. He is not the Federal High Court, the Attorney-General of the Federation or the commander of the security agencies. It is legitimate to demand that he raise issues in the Senate, engage relevant authorities and advocate for justice. It is, however, misleading to assign him executive or judicial powers he does not possess. Accountability requires that every institution be examined according to its constitutional responsibility. This is why the Okuama issue should not become a political contest between individual politicians. Rather than exploiting the suffering of Okuama for electoral advantage, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege and other Urhobo leaders and stakeholders should pool their influence, contacts and resources to sustain constructive pressure and dialogue with the authorities. The people of Okuama need solutions, not competing political narratives over who has done more or less. The questions that matter are bigger than Dafinone. Who authorised the continued detention of the affected citizens? Under what legal authority were they held? Were they charged before a competent court? Why has a reported judicial order for their release allegedly not been implemented? Which institutions are responsible for enforcing the order? These are the questions that can produce genuine accountability. Delta Central voters are entitled to scrutinise Dafinone’s legislative record, constituency interventions, motions, visibility and effectiveness ahead of 2027. If he fails where the Constitution empowers him to act, he should be criticised. If his interventions produce no results, he should be asked to explain. But he should not be blamed for powers constitutionally vested in other institutions. Okuama deserves justice, its families deserve answers, and the community deserves healing and reconstruction. Every institution involved must be held accountable. But accountability without constitutional clarity becomes political theatre, while criticism without factual discipline risks becoming blackmail. If there is a valid court order, it must be obeyed. If there is unlawful detention, it must end. If officials violated the law, they must answer. And if institutions failed, they must be held responsible. If Senator Dafinone is to be judged, let him be judged for what the Constitution empowers a senator to do—and for what the evidence shows he actually did. Okuama deserves justice, not convenient narratives; Delta Central deserves accountability, not scapegoating; and the truth deserves a voice, even when it is politically inconvenient. Ufuoma Egbe, A Public Affairs Analyst writes from Eku, Delta State. The post Okuama: When Political Blame Ignores the Constitution, Fuels Blackmail appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Real Betis : Pellegrini pousse pour le retour de Sofyan Amrabat
items.description: À quelques jours de la fermeture du mercato, le Betis Séville n’a pas abandonné la piste Sofyan Amrabat. L’entraîneur Manuel Pellegrini souhaite en priorité recruter un milieu défensif et verrait d’un très bon œil le retour de l’international marocain, prêté au club andalou la saison dernière. Selon le quotidien espagnol AS, le technicien chilien considère le recrutement d’un véritable récupérateur comme la priorité de cette fin de mercato. Et parmi les profils étudiés, Amrabat conserve une place privilégiée. Pellegrini connaît parfaitement les qualités du Marocain. Lors de son passage au Betis la saison dernière, Amrabat avait notamment séduit par son impact dans les duels, son expérience et sa capacité à assurer l’équilibre de l’équipe. Pellegrini estime donc qu’il lui manque encore un milieu défensif capable d'apporter davantage de présence et de sécurité devant la défense. Le retour d’Amrabat reste toutefois loin d’être acquis. Le Marocain est actuellement sous contrat avec Fenerbahçe et s’entraînerait à l’écart du groupe, alors qu’il cherche une solution pour son avenir. Autre obstacle majeur : son salaire, jugé élevé pour les finances du Betis. Le club andalou doit également gérer plusieurs dossiers, notamment celui du retour de Dani Ceballos, et pourrait être contraint de réaliser plusieurs départs avant de pouvoir recruter. Malgré les difficultés financières et contractuelles, Pellegrini continue donc de pousser pour Amrabat. Le technicien chilien apprécie particulièrement le fait que le Marocain connaisse déjà le club, le championnat et ses méthodes de travail. The post Real Betis : Pellegrini pousse pour le retour de Sofyan Amrabat appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Prof. Bano Barry sur la fraude aux examens nationaux : « en Guinée, on a cinq acteurs de la fraude »
items.description: Screenshot " data-large-file="https://i0.wp.com/mediaguinee.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/IMG_7250.jpeg?fit=1024%2C535&ssl=1" /> Invité de l’émission “Guinée Today” de Télé 24, l’ancien ministre de l’Éducation nationale du régime déchu, le professeur Alpha Amadou Bano Barry, s’est prononcé sur la fraude enregistrée lors des examens nationaux et sur les différents acteurs qui y seraient impliqués. « En Guinée, on a cinq acteurs de la fraude. Le premier, ce sont certains responsables de la chaîne des examens, du sommet à la base, qui sont impliqués dans la fraude. Deuxièmement, certains enseignants, ceux qui organisent les groupes de révision et qui, après, créent les groupes WhatsApp avec des tickets d’entrée, sont aussi impliqués dans la fraude. Troisième catégorie : certains enseignants utilisés au niveau de la surveillance, au niveau du secrétariat du centre, du secrétariat au moment de la correction, c’est-à-dire le découpage des en-têtes, la mise en place des PV, la saisie manuelle des notes, la saisie informatique des notes. Certains des enseignants impliqués à ce niveau sont impliqués dans la fraude », a déclaré le professeur Bano Barry dans l’émission Today du mercredi 19 août 2026. Poursuivant, il a ajouté : « Vous avez certains parents d’élèves qui sont à la fois bénéficiaires. En fait, il y a des enseignants qui les démarchent. Eux-mêmes démarchent souvent des enseignants pour pouvoir faire frauder leurs propres enfants. Et puis, vous avez les élèves, les élèves eux-mêmes. » Parlant de la dangerosité des différentes formes de fraude, l’enseignant-chercheur a précisé : « Alors, la fraude la moins dangereuse, c’est la fraude des élèves qui ne sont pas dans des groupes WhatsApp. Comme je l’ai dit, tous les élèves, y compris moi, Bano, parce que quand j’ai organisé le bac en 2021, ils ont dit : “Bac, B-A-C, on a dit Bano aussi a copié.” Je suis venu parfois avec des petits bouts de papier dans ma poche, dans l’espoir que la formule-là, je vais la retrouver. Ça, ce n’est pas très grave. En réalité, ça existe, ça existait, ça existera toujours. Demandez au voisin quand on sait qu’il est meilleur que vous en chimie, vous voulez savoir quelle est la formule. Il vous dit, il fait ça, après il fait comme ça, V, pour vous dire que c’est V4, ça existe. Que le meilleur candidat, en sortant, laisse tomber son brouillon, en faisant semblant qu’il l’a oublié, alors qu’en réalité, il l’a délibérément fait, tout ça, ça existe », a-t-il rappelé. Enfin, le professeur Bano Barry a conclu : « Les plus dangereux sont ceux qui sont dans la fraude informatique et les triplants. » Elisa CAMARA L’article Prof. Bano Barry sur la fraude aux examens nationaux : « en Guinée, on a cinq acteurs de la fraude » est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .

items.title: Tompolo’s ‘manumission’ mission, the ironies and the joys of life
items.description: By ENEWARIDIDEKE EKANPOU The state of being swept into oblivion after a sacrificial engagement to free a people from developmental enslavement sounds retrogressive and meaningless. It sounds retrogressive and meaningless because it has no historical bequest to inspire and guide the next generations away from the path that once convulsed their entire existence like the deadly constrictions of a python. This is a state of being a vassal to obscurity – which is far beyond the contemplation of a true freedom fighter. Activist. Advocate. As a hawk would do to the children of a mother-hen, obscurity would have long swooped on Tompolo as a vassal after his glorious history of freedom struggles in the Niger Delta but for the occasional skirmishes between haulers and hailers who have respectively positioned themselves in the life of Tompolo. So from time to time ripples are created by haulers and hailers in the life of Tompolo. Tompolo needs haulers as much as he needs hailers who interpret him using varied lenses. To speak without waters kept in the mouth, devoid of ballooned jaws, the haulers are indeed pathologically excited by destruction and lies while the hailers are governed and excited by construction and truth in the life of Tompolo as regards the manumission struggle. For the haulers, specifically, allegations of non-performance impetuously levelled against Tompolo and Tantita Security Services Nigeria Limited constitute a piece of deadwood in their hands, carried and deposited on every doorstep with amazing ease and agility, without any restraining conscience. No one interprets Tompolo better than the haulers and the hailers given his performance. These are haulers and hailers whose beloved activities have uncannily created a kind of symbiosis in the life of Tompolo, as their activities oppositionally take two different routes and later merge into one when sufficiently awakened. Differently, these haulers and hailers are driven majorly by benightedness and re-awakening in their oppositional engagements. The first dance of a hauler is to throw stones at a High Chief, Dr. Government Oweizide Ekpemupolo Tompolo. The attraction, the inclination, the predilection for this deadly dance could be borne out of pure misunderstanding and benightedness; it could equally be borne out of envy and dreams of hegemony extended to the border from which Tompolo operates without being a threat to the known symbolic borders. Where Tompolo sees his operational border as a site to interact meaningfully and integrate people to actualise their varied dreams in life, the pureblind haulers only ignite the borders through hegemonic calculations situated in unseating Tompolo through deadly stones thrown at his development efforts and reputation. Ironically, these haulers become hailers in their moment of epistemological awakening. At this moment they realise and recognise that they have wronged Tompolo in the past when they threw stones drunkenly without a known transgression committed by Tompolo. From Saul to Paul, these haulers labour daily to remove the stains they had ignorantly planted on Tompolo’s name. These are the unstoppable haulers who have sworn to themselves individually never to err on the path of deadly stone-throwing. There are also hailers who are hailers without any metamorphosis. They are the core believers who inhale and exhale Tompolo right from the Garden of Eden. These hailers occupy a class higher than the hailer-turned-haulers. Sometimes haulers and hailers switch positions. It is great when haulers become hailers because this is purely a product of dialectical thinking, aided by epistemological awakening. With open hands haulers must be admitted. It is dangerous when hailers become haulers because this is purely a demonic metamorphosis borne out of envy, ingratitude and malediction, driven by deflection from the principle of appreciation expected of a normal human being whose faculties are still healthy. The metamorphosis from haulers to hailers is rationally commendable; but the metamorphosis from hailers to haulers is illogical, irrational and condemnable because it is rooted in ingratitude and unhealthy desires and expectations from a mere mortal whose capabilities have their own cosmically defined limitations. This metamorphosis occurs because the hailers fail to recognise the limitations of Tompolo’s capabilities. This metamorphosis occurs because the hailers see Tompolo as God who can meet all the demands and expectations of man however complex and irrational. When this illogical characterisation of Tompolo does not come to reality, the hailers turn haulers and throw deadly stones at Tompolo’s reputation. This is the time they imaginatively create stories that are even too childish to be told as folktales. The hailer-turned-haulers of Tompolo are the plague of this society. They are a plague more lethal than COVID-19 and Ebola because they are epidemiologically beyond any medical prevention or arrest as they pose a grave danger and challenge to modern medical science. They constitute a new medical phenomenon that demands research to know if endoscopy, biopsy and laboratory analyses could be scientifically drawn on to detect the constant affliction of these haulers and hailers which predisposes them to mutation between haulers and hailers in their public pronouncements targeted at Tompolo and Tantita. Sadly, Nigeria does not have such medical facilities to confront the constant affliction of these haulers and hailers. The only hope lies in deliberately created distance from such haulers. A quarantine, maybe, if it could be activated and enforced! Such distances must be congenitally created so the imaginative powers of these haulers and hailers would be emasculated from birth. Those who had associated with Tompolo and enjoyed him to the fullest in every dimension are today the haulers who daily anchor the anti-Tompolo propaganda from the creeks of the Niger Delta to the roads, flyovers and cities of Nigeria. To demarket Tompolo and to demarket Tantita is their daily obsession. They are not telling the public that their media campaign against Tompolo is not borne out of Tompolo’s insensitivity to their plight, but is borne out of their desire to unseat and take over his position even where they lack the capacity and moral purity. It is a media campaign borne out of envy but they would not reveal this to the public. From the camp of hailers they have shifted to the camp of haulers in pursuit of their own selfish ends. Those who were once loyal to Tompolo belong to this obsessional class of haulers on rampage everywhere like ravenous wolves looking for people to devour. Some persons have shamelessly become objects of mutation in Nigeria. Those who have moved from hailers to haulers, ravenously poised to gore and devour people, are the Judas Iscariots of our time who were once with Tompolo working as devoted disciples. However, these haulers collude and labour to demarket Tompolo and Tantita; they shall not be believed because they are traitors who are merely envious of Tompolo and his unbeatable achievements in Nigeria. Known to the public is the fact that among the haulers of Tompolo we know of no one who was not a beneficiary of Tompolo. This means the media campaign is a product of betrayal and envy. To move from hailer to hauler shows Tompolo is originally a good man who has no haulers but who only had haulers when the hailers became suddenly afflicted by the virus called Judas Iscariot. The moral purity, the spiritual purity, the goodness, the commendable steadfastness of Tompolo is foregrounded when the haulers and the hailers of Tompolo skirmish from time to time. With the height attained by Tompolo in the ‘manumission’ struggle, skirmishes between haulers and hailers are expected. Without the cauldron heated by the skirmishes between the two oppositional forces of haulers and hailers, Tompolo would be a vassal to obscurity. From the skirmishes the public become more clearly awakened to the true compositions of the haulers and the hailers and align themselves with the positive forces of Tompolo – who are the hailers. However, as they skirmish from time to time, it is the haulers who have turned hailers that must be believed. To be believed also are those who have been hailers without a shift of position from their original spot right from the cradle of Tompolo’s manumission struggle. Life rhythmically strikes a dull note when it is devoid of ironies. Part of the joys of life lies in its ironies. Tompolo’s entire life is devoted to the struggle to free Niger Deltans from chains of oppression, exploitation, enslavement and underdevelopment. After all these sacrifices, it is the constant skirmishes between the haulers and the hailers that have popularised the performance story of Tompolo and Tantita Security Services Limited Nigeria in Nigeria. Whenever the haulers and the hailers are at war, that Tompolo and Tantita are doing a great job is always clearly communicated to Nigerians. It is interestingly ironical that Tompolo’s manumission struggle is daily crowned with ennoblement and commendation whenever the haulers and the hailers skirmish on the media space for recognition and judgment of the public. Tompolo and Tantita should no longer be bothered by the activities of the haulers and the hailers anywhere on earth because they are their best promoters. They are their best promoters because Nigerians have known that the haulers of Tompolo and Tantita are inveterate liars driven by selfish calculations in their sustained media campaign. At this time we are confronted by recollections of haulers like Ezebu Danbalaowei, Azuzu Shooter, Ogogorowei, Tebe Embeleowei, Gbanaghaowei and Nomowei Edebu who were the greatest beneficiaries of Tompolo and Tantita yesterday but who are today shameless haulers. The post Tompolo’s ‘manumission’ mission, the ironies and the joys of life appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: The Nigerian dream: Is it still alive? By Ejiro Ofoye
items.description: There is a question that Nigerians do not ask often enough, perhaps because the answer frightens us. Is the Nigerian Dream still alive? Not the dream politicians describe at rallies. Not the Nigeria of campaign posters, television advertisements and carefully prepared speeches. I mean the ordinary Nigerian dream-the quiet hope of a father who wants his children to live better than he did; the hope of a young graduate that his certificate will lead to a decent job; the hope of a trader that her business will grow; the hope of a farmer that he can return safely from his farm; the hope of a worker that his salary will last beyond the first week of the month. For generations, Nigerians believed that if they worked hard, educated their children and remained determined, they could build a respectable life. That belief is being tested. The question we must ask as a nation is no longer whether Nigerians still dream. They certainly do. The more troubling question is whether Nigeria still provides enough opportunities for those dreams to become reality. Nigeria remains a country of enormous potential. We have a large and youthful population, vast agricultural opportunities, abundant natural resources, a vibrant entrepreneurial culture and a generation of young people competing successfully on the global stage. Yet potential is not prosperity. For millions of Nigerians, daily life has become a struggle to keep up with the rising cost of food, transportation, housing, electricity, healthcare and education. Recent reporting indicates that although Nigeria’s economic reforms have improved investor confidence and some macroeconomic indicators, the benefits have not yet translated into meaningful relief for many households. That contradiction deserves our attention. What does economic growth mean to a family that cannot afford three decent meals a day? What does a rising stock market mean to the young Nigerian who has never owned a single share? What does improved foreign investment mean to the graduate who has spent years searching for a decent job? These are not merely economic questions. They are questions about the Nigerian Dream itself. Nigeria’s economy is showing signs of greater stability. The International Monetary Fund projects real GDP growth of about 4.1 percent for 2026 and says recent reforms have strengthened macroeconomic stability and external buffers. These developments should be acknowledged. Nigeria cannot build a sustainable future without macroeconomic stability. Reforms that improve government finances, strengthen the foreign-exchange market, attract investment and encourage production are necessary. But economic statistics must ultimately serve human beings. A stable economy that does not improve household welfare cannot be the final destination. That is why the success of economic policy should not only be measured by investor confidence. It must also be measured by the confidence of ordinary Nigerians that tomorrow can genuinely be better than today. Perhaps nowhere is the crisis of confidence more visible than among Nigerian youths. Across the country, young people are asking themselves a difficult question: Should I build my future here or seek my future elsewhere? The phenomenon popularly known as “Japa” is more than a migration trend. It is a reflection of aspiration, frustration and the search for opportunity. We should not condemn Nigerians who leave in search of better opportunities. There is nothing unpatriotic about wanting a decent life. The problem begins when leaving becomes the preferred expression of hope. A country should not export its brightest young people because it cannot create enough space for their dreams at home. Yet, even in the middle of this crisis of confidence, Nigeria continues to produce extraordinary stories. Our young people are building technology companies, creating music that travels across continents, developing businesses from tiny rooms, competing in global professional fields and inventing solutions to problems that should have been solved by government. The Nigerian spirit has not disappeared. If anything, it has become more stubborn. But resilience should not become an excuse for governmental failure. We cannot continue telling Nigerians to be resilient when what they need is a functioning system. A young entrepreneur does not need another speech about resilience when the cost of credit is prohibitive. A manufacturer does not need another seminar on productivity when electricity remains unreliable. A farmer does not need a motivational message when insecurity prevents him from reaching his farm. A graduate does not need another certificate when there are no productive opportunities waiting for him. Consider electricity. Nigeria is talking about electric vehicles and a cleaner transportation future while the country’s electricity system remains severely inadequate. The country is delivering only a fraction of the power required by a population of more than 200 million people, leaving households and businesses heavily dependent on petrol and diesel generators. There is something almost poetic about that contradiction. We want electric cars, but many Nigerians cannot reliably power their homes. We want digital transformation, but businesses spend heavily generating their own electricity. We want industrialisation, but factories struggle with the cost of energy. We want to compete with the world, while many of our businesses first have to solve the basic problem of keeping the lights on. The Nigerian Dream cannot be powered by generators alone. And then there is security. What is the value of economic opportunity if people cannot safely enjoy it? When communities are attacked, farms abandoned, businesses disrupted and families displaced, insecurity becomes more than a security problem. It becomes an economic problem and, ultimately, a problem for the Nigerian Dream. A farmer cannot dream when he is afraid to enter his farm. A child cannot dream properly when school is unsafe. A business cannot grow when its owner fears kidnapping. A community cannot prosper when its people are constantly looking over their shoulders. Security is therefore not merely one item on the government’s agenda. Security is the foundation upon which every other national ambition rests. This is why the Nigerian Dream cannot be reduced to GDP. A country’s economy may grow while its people remain anxious. The stock market may rise while millions remain outside the capital market. Foreign investors may become more confident while ordinary citizens struggle to obtain affordable credit. This is the Nigeria of two realities. One Nigeria is attracting investors. Another Nigeria is borrowing to survive. One Nigeria is discussing billion-dollar investments. Another Nigeria is asking how to pay school fees. One Nigeria is celebrating economic indicators. Another Nigeria is counting the days until the next salary. Both are real. Our challenge is to make them one Nigeria. That is the real test of economic reform. Reform should not be judged only by whether government finances look healthier or whether investors are optimistic. Those things matter. But eventually, the question must reach the Nigerian home. Is life becoming better? Can a worker save? Can a young couple afford a home? Can a graduate find meaningful employment? Can a small business obtain affordable credit? Can a farmer produce without fear? Can a child receive quality education without the family entering crippling debt? Can a sick Nigerian receive treatment without selling everything the family owns? These are the questions that will determine whether the Nigerian Dream is alive. And as we approach another general election, these questions must become more important than political slogans. The 2027 election must not become another contest of who can make the loudest promises. It must become a referendum on ideas, competence, character and performance. Nigerians must ask every politician a simple question: What exactly will you do to make my life better? Not what will you say. Not what will you promise. What will you do? We have spent decades changing governments without sufficiently changing the conditions under which ordinary Nigerians live. Perhaps the time has come to change the way we measure leadership. A governor should not be judged primarily by the number of projects commissioned, but by the quality of life of the people. A minister should not be judged by the number of conferences attended, but by measurable improvements in the sector. A president should not be judged only by economic statistics, but by whether the citizen at the bottom of the economic ladder can look into the future without fear. Leadership is ultimately about human beings. And the Nigerian Dream is ultimately about human dignity. There is also a responsibility on citizens. We cannot demand a better Nigeria while celebrating corruption when it benefits us. We cannot condemn electoral malpractice and then sell our votes. We cannot demand good leadership while supporting leaders because of ethnicity, religion, political connections or immediate financial rewards. We cannot complain about the country and then abandon our responsibility to build it. Nation-building is not the exclusive responsibility of government. But government has the greater responsibility because government controls the institutions, policies and resources that determine the environment in which citizens live. The Nigerian Dream is therefore a shared responsibility-but leadership must lead. So, is the Nigerian Dream dead? No. But it is wounded. It is alive in the student who still believes education can change his life. It is alive in the entrepreneur who refuses to close her business. It is alive in the farmer who returns to his land after hardship. It is alive in the Nigerian doctor, engineer, lawyer, teacher, soldier, civil servant, artisan and professional who wakes up every morning and continues to serve. It is alive in the Nigerian in Lagos, Abuja, Kano, Enugu, Port Harcourt, Benin, Ibadan, Maiduguri, Warri and hundreds of smaller communities who still believe that this country can be better. The Nigerian Dream has survived military rule, economic crises, political instability, corruption, insecurity and years of disappointment. But survival is not enough. We must make the dream attainable again. We must build an economy where hard work is rewarded. We must create jobs rather than merely celebrate employment statistics. We must make electricity reliable enough for businesses to plan. We must secure our farms, roads and communities. We must reform education so that our young people are prepared not merely to look for jobs but to create value. We must strengthen institutions so that the rule of law is not dependent on who you know. We must make public office a place of service rather than a shortcut to private wealth. And we must build a political culture in which competence matters more than propaganda. Nigeria does not lack wealth. Nigeria does not lack talent. Nigeria does not lack ideas. Nigeria does not lack hardworking people. What Nigeria lacks is the consistent conversion of these advantages into shared prosperity. That is the unfinished business of our nation. The Nigerian Dream should never mean that every Nigerian must become rich. It should mean something more fundamental: that every Nigerian who works honestly should have a fair chance to live with dignity; that every child should have a reasonable opportunity to rise; that where you are born should not determine how far you can go; and that leaving Nigeria should be a choice-not an escape route from hopelessness. The dream is still alive. But it is asking something of us. It is asking for leadership with courage. It is asking for citizens with conscience. It is asking for institutions with integrity. It is asking for an economy that serves people, not merely numbers. And above all, it is asking whether we are prepared to stop speaking endlessly about Nigeria’s potential and finally begin delivering on it. Perhaps that is the most important question before us. Not whether Nigeria can become great. We already know she can. The question is whether we have the courage, discipline and leadership to make greatness possible. The Nigerian Dream is still alive. But Nigerians should no longer be asked merely to dream. They deserve the opportunity to live the dream. *Dr Ofoye writes from Lagos. The post The Nigerian dream: Is it still alive? By Ejiro Ofoye appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: FG releases 2026/2027 Unity Schools admission list
items.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Government has released the 2026/2027 admission list for successful candidates offered admission into Junior Secondary School One (JSS1) of Federal Unity Colleges across the country. The admission release, approved by the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, marks the commencement of the admission process for candidates seeking entry into the nation’s Federal Unity Colleges for the new academic session. The Federal Ministry of Education, in a statement issued by its Director of Press and Public Relations, Folasade Boriowo, said the development was in line with the government’s commitment to ensuring a transparent, accessible and orderly admission process. According to the ministry, parents and guardians can now check the admission status of their children and wards through the Federal Ministry of Education’s admission portal or the notice board of the relevant Federal Unity College. It directed successful candidates to print their admission slips and proceed to the Federal Unity College indicated on the slips for confirmation and completion of admission formalities. The ministry specifically directed parents and guardians to access the admission status and print admission slips through the FME Posting Portal at https://fmeposting.com.ng/auth/login. It urged parents and guardians to check the admission status of their children and wards promptly and ensure that successful candidates report to their respective colleges as required. The minister congratulated all successful candidates on securing admission into the Federal Unity Colleges and urged them to approach their academic journey with diligence, discipline and a strong commitment to excellence. The Federal Unity Colleges are among the Federal Government’s key institutions for promoting quality secondary education while fostering national integration by bringing students from diverse parts of the country together. The release of the 2026/2027 admission list clears the way for successful candidates to commence the next stage of their secondary education in Unity Colleges nationwide. The post FG releases 2026/2027 Unity Schools admission list appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Burkina Faso : Les groupes terroristes recourent à l'enrôlement de mineurs
items.description: Les groupes terroristes recourent de plus en plus à l'enrôlement de mineurs pour tenter de compenser les lourdes pertes qu'ils subissent face aux forces combattantes au Burkina Faso. C'est ce que rapporte l'Agence d'information du Burkina (AIB), ce lundi 24 août 2026. Selon l'AIB, des enfants parfois âgés de 10 à 14 ans sont recrutés, formés à la hâte et utilisés pour diverses missions, notamment comme guetteurs, espions, opérateurs radio ou combattants. Le recrutement s'appuie sur la vulnérabilité des enfants. Les groupes armés exploitent notamment leur naïveté, leur situation de précarité ou leur peur pour les enrôler, parfois par la ruse et parfois sous la contrainte. Le Groupe de soutien à l'islam et aux musulmans (GSIM) est notamment présenté comme particulièrement actif dans cette pratique. Les enfants peuvent être affectés à des missions de surveillance, de collecte d'informations ou de transmission de renseignements. Leur jeune âge peut permettre aux groupes armés de les faire circuler plus facilement dans certaines localités sans éveiller immédiatement les soupçons. Les conditions dans lesquelles ces enfants évoluent restent particulièrement difficiles. Les chefs terroristes, confrontés à des difficultés pour assurer leurs propres besoins, peinent à fournir une alimentation et des soins convenables aux mineurs enrôlés. Ils peuvent également les abandonner lorsqu'une opération des forces combattantes intervient, privilégiant leur propre fuite. Des opérations de démantèlement de bases terroristes ont ainsi permis aux forces armées burkinabè de récupérer plusieurs mineurs. Certains enfants, âgés de 10 à 14 ans, ont livré des témoignages faisant état des violences et des conditions difficiles auxquelles ils auraient été soumis. Au-delà de la lutte contre les groupes armés, le phénomène pose donc un important enjeu de protection de l'enfance. La récupération de ces mineurs par les forces combattantes ouvre la voie à leur mise à l'abri et à une prise en charge adaptée à leur situation. L'enrôlement de mineurs rappelle enfin la nécessité d'une vigilance accrue des familles et des communautés face aux stratégies de recrutement des groupes terroristes. La protection des enfants apparaît ainsi comme un enjeu indissociable de la reconquête et de la sécurisation des territoires. Lefaso.net Source : AIB

Les travaux de cette 1ʳᵉ session se sont poursuivis par l’ouverture des assises du parlement de la confédération de l'AES, présidées par le Premier ministre du Niger, Ali Mahaman Lamine Zeine, représentant le Président de la République, le Général d’armée Abdourahamane Tiani. items.title: Secteur minier : La CIMR franchit un cap en prenant le contrôle conjoint de la CMT
items.description: Un fonds de retraite peut-il devenir un acteur de premier plan dans la gouvernance d’une entreprise minière cotée ? La question s’impose à la lumière de la récente opération validée par le Conseil de la concurrence, qui consacre l’entrée de la Caisse interprofessionnelle marocaine de retraite (CIMR) dans une nouvelle phase de sa stratégie d’investissement. L’autorité de régulation a en effet autorisé une opération de concentration économique qui redessine l’actionnariat de la Compagnie Minière de Touissit (CMT), l’un des groupes historiques du secteur minier marocain. Par cette décision, la CIMR ne se contente plus d’un rôle d’actionnaire financier. Elle devient, aux côtés du groupe émirati Ayrad Group Limited , copropriétaire exerçant un contrôle conjoint sur une société cotée à la Bourse de Casablanca. Le 13 juillet 2026, la commission permanente du Conseil de la concurrence, présidée par Ahmed Rahhou, a donné son accord à cette opération de concentration économique. La décision porte sur la prise de contrôle conjoint de la CMT par Ayrad Group Limited et la CIMR, ouvrant ainsi la voie à son entrée en vigueur sur le plan juridique. Cette validation intervient plusieurs mois après les premières démarches réglementaires. Le 7 mai 2026, le Conseil de la concurrence avait publié un avis relatif à la notification de l’opération, mettant à la disposition du public un résumé des informations communiquées par les parties concernées. Le document identifiait les acquéreurs comme étant Ayrad Group Limited et la Caisse interprofessionnelle marocaine de retraite, tandis que la société visée était la Compagnie Minière de Touissit S.A. La nature de l’opération consistait en une prise de contrôle conjoint dans le secteur de l’industrie minière, plus particulièrement dans l’activité de production de concentrés de plomb et de zinc contenant de l’argent. L’opération s’inscrit dans un processus amorcé plusieurs mois auparavant. En mars 2026, le groupe Ayrad , basé aux Émirats arabes unis, avait acquis l’intégralité des participations détenues par le fonds OSEAD Fund dans le cadre d’une transaction évaluée à 130 millions de dollars. Cette acquisition avait permis au groupe de prendre indirectement le contrôle de 37,04 % du capital de la société minière marocaine, tout en mettant un terme à plusieurs contentieux judiciaires qui entouraient l’entreprise. La nouvelle architecture capitalistique prévoit désormais un partage du contrôle entre les deux investisseurs. Ayrad Group conservera une participation de 37,04 % dans le capital de la CMT, tandis que la CIMR renforcera sa présence en portant sa part de 14,41 % à 16,12 %. Cette évolution ouvre également une nouvelle séquence réglementaire. Elle prépare le terrain au lancement d’une offre publique d’achat obligatoire (OPA) portant sur le reste des actions de la CMT cotées en Bourse, sous réserve de l’obtention d’une autorisation supplémentaire de l’Autorité marocaine du marché des capitaux (AMMC). Au-delà de l’aspect strictement juridique, l’opération suscite l’intérêt des observateurs financiers en raison du rôle joué par la CIMR. Pourquoi un fonds de retraite décide-t-il de dépasser le statut d’investisseur minoritaire pour participer directement au contrôle d’une entreprise industrielle ? La réponse réside d’abord dans la nature des actifs concernés. Les fonds de retraite sont soumis à des engagements de long terme vis-à-vis de leurs affiliés et cherchent à faire coïncider leurs placements avec ces obligations futures. Dans cette perspective, le secteur minier présente plusieurs atouts : des flux de trésorerie potentiellement stables, une capacité de distribution de dividendes et une visibilité à long terme susceptible de soutenir les rendements nécessaires au financement des pensions. L’investissement dans les matières premières constitue également une forme de protection contre l’inflation. Les métaux exploités par la Compagnie Minière de Touissit – notamment le plomb, le zinc et l’argent – évoluent en fonction des cycles économiques mondiaux. Leur valorisation permet ainsi de préserver, dans une certaine mesure, le pouvoir d’achat des actifs détenus par le fonds de retraite. Le choix de la CIMR répond aussi à une logique de gouvernance. En devenant copropriétaire exerçant un contrôle conjoint, le fonds pourra participer plus directement aux décisions stratégiques de l’entreprise à travers les instances dirigeantes. Une telle implication est généralement perçue comme un moyen de renforcer les exigences en matière de transparence, de protection des actionnaires et de gestion rationnelle des ressources. Cette présence institutionnelle pourrait également contribuer à stabiliser l’actionnariat de la société. Pour les marchés financiers, l’association entre un investisseur industriel comme Ayrad Group et un fonds de retraite de premier plan constitue un signal de confiance. Elle est susceptible de réduire les risques opérationnels, d’attirer davantage d’investisseurs institutionnels et de limiter les mouvements spéculatifs pouvant affecter le titre. L’opération apparaît ainsi comme bien plus qu’un simple réaménagement du capital de la CMT. Elle illustre une évolution plus profonde du rôle des grands investisseurs institutionnels marocains, désormais davantage enclins à exercer une influence directe sur les entreprises dans lesquelles ils investissent. Pour la CIMR, cette prise de contrôle conjoint marque une étape supplémentaire dans une stratégie orientée vers un « investissement institutionnel actif », visant à mobiliser l’épargne nationale au profit de secteurs productifs jugés stratégiques. Une orientation qui accompagne, en filigrane, les ambitions de développement industriel et de souveraineté économique portées par le Maroc dans les activités extractives et minières. items.title: Benjamin Netanyahu affirme que l’Iran a tenté de tuer l’un de ses fils
items.description: Benjamin Netanyahu a accusé lundi l’Iran d’avoir tenté de tuer l’un de ses deux fils, sans préciser lequel ni fournir davantage de détails sur les circonstances de cette attaque présumée. Lors d’un entretien téléphonique avec la chaîne israélienne Channel 14, le Premier ministre israélien a déclaré : « L’Iran a pris pour cible l’un de mes fils. L’Iran a essayé de tuer un de mes fils. » Cette accusation intervient alors qu’Israël reste confronté à de fortes tensions sécuritaires avec l’Iran. Le chef du gouvernement israélien s’exprimait notamment au sujet d’informations selon lesquelles le Shin Bet, le service de sécurité intérieure israélien, aurait refusé d’accorder une protection rapprochée permanente à Gadi Eisenkot, ancien chef d’état-major et principal rival politique de Netanyahu à l’approche des élections législatives prévues le 27 octobre. Netanyahu s’est prononcé en faveur d’une protection permanente pour Eisenkot, estimant qu’elle ne constituait « pas un luxe ». « Sans cela, les Iraniens réussiront » , a-t-il déclaré. Benjamin Netanyahu est père de trois enfants, deux fils et une fille. Il n’a pas précisé lequel de ses fils aurait été visé par cette tentative présumée. Son fils aîné, Yair Netanyahu, 35 ans, séjourne depuis plusieurs années régulièrement aux États-Unis, notamment en Floride, où il bénéficierait de la protection du Shin Bet. Sa présence à Miami a déjà suscité des critiques en Israël concernant le coût de cette protection pour les contribuables, certains habitants de Floride ayant également exprimé leur inquiétude face au risque de voir la région devenir une cible. Peu après les déclarations de Netanyahu, le journaliste israélien Amit Segal a affirmé sur sa chaîne Telegram que la tentative d’assassinat présumée était connue depuis « des mois », mais qu’une interdiction de publication aurait empêché sa révélation jusqu’à présent. À ce stade, les autorités israéliennes n’ont fourni aucun détail permettant de vérifier publiquement les accusations formulées par Benjamin Netanyahu contre l’Iran. items.title: Trump Is Losing Touch With the Public
items.description: This is an edition of The Atlantic Daily, a newsletter that guides you through the biggest stories of the day, helps you discover new ideas, and recommends the best in culture. Sign up for it here. One of the few issues that unites voters and politicians of both parties right now is data centers. Three-quarters of Americans would oppose a data center being built near where they live, according to a new poll released last week by Heatmap Pro and Embold Research. The two leading lights of the left, Representative Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Senator Bernie Sanders, have sponsored a bill in Congress to create a temporary moratorium on new centers. They have an unlikely ally in archconservative Governor Greg Abbott of Texas, who said yesterday on ABC’s This Week that data-center companies “basically dug their own grave” and “got the backlash they deserve.” Standing against this consensus is Donald Trump. The president remains a big booster of data centers. “Communities that don’t take a data center—they’re making a mistake,” he said Thursday during an interview with his on-again, off-again lackey Michael Cohen. “Data centers throw off tremendous amounts of jobs and money.” This was no one-off. Trump had made several similar comments recently. “If I were the mayor of a town or the governor of a state and I had a chance to get a big plant in, an AI plant or a data center, I would absolutely want it, because the jobs are enormous and the money paid, the taxes paid, are just enormous,” Trump said last week—although he allowed that the sector could use “a little public-relations help.” This puts Trump, the most successful demagogue in American political history, in the unusual position of misreading, and opposing, a populist groundswell. During his 2016 presidential campaign, Trump took many stands that were unpopular among establishment politicians. Some of these positions put him at odds not only with Democrats but also with most Republican elected officials. Trump broke with Republicans in claiming that he would protect social-welfare programs such as Medicare and Social Security, and he broke a bipartisan consensus by attacking free-trade agreements and promising protectionism. On these matters (as well as on his willingness to encourage and participate in gutter racism ), Trump demonstrated that a big constituency existed for views that other politicians had deemed electoral liabilities. Data centers’ political arc has been different. Initially, many officials seemed to back the centers, following exactly Trump’s logic: They offered jobs and tax benefits. But as public opinion turned—driven by a mix of backlash to AI in general, environmental concerns, worries about energy prices, and old-fashioned NIMBYism— politicians changed their view as well . Why has Trump missed the shift? Presumably one reason is that he is surrounded by advisers and tech executives such as David Sacks and Larry Ellison , who are major boosters of and players in the industry. Tech companies invested heavily in Trump at the start of his second administration, lavishing him with gifts, including a gold-plated bauble and donations to projects such as his inauguration and his ballroom, and Trump has reciprocated by taking policy stances that benefit them. Trump may also be personally profiting from the AI boom; his financial disclosures show he’s become more of a tech investor . Trump has always tended to adopt the latest thing he’s heard, no matter what it is. He has been willing to alienate corporate interests in the past—when he saw some political upside. But he is not hearing from voters who might alert him to how unpopular data centers are. Trump’s rallies and speeches once created a feedback loop in which he conveyed his message to voters and—crucially—they conveyed their thoughts to him. Now, as his energy sinks, his travel schedule gets lighter, and security makes events more challenging, Trump is getting out less . Though his stump speeches dragged on for hours, Trump was carefully attuned to audience attention and what did and didn’t work. “You know, if it gets a little boring, if I see people starting to sort of, maybe thinking about leaving, I can sort of tell the audience, I just say, ‘We will build the wall!’ and they go nuts,” he told The New York Times in 2016. I think often about a speech Trump delivered in July 2022. It was billed as the launch of a new policy agenda, but as he read it, both Trump and his audience seemed bored. Then he ad-libbed a riff about trans athletes and the crowd came alive. Trump picked up on the shift and emphasized it; trans issues would become a central talking point for his 2024 campaign. The president has always been susceptible to fake news and bad at filtering information, but rallies provided a gut check about his base, if not about the broader national reality. Now Trump isn’t even receiving that kind of information. One of his major conduits for information is Natalie Harp , a sycophantic aide who isn’t interested in exposing Trump to criticism. He could read public-opinion data, but as his own approval sinks, he has taken to saying (and may well believe) that polls are fake. As his world shrinks, Trump’s populist touch has faded. Despite being elected twice on an antiwar platform, he’s launched attacks on Venezuela and Iran. As the Iran war has gotten bogged down, he’s been incapable of reading the public mood. He has dismissed voter frustration over rising fuel costs, saying “I don’t even think about” gas; he previously called affordability a “hoax.” In response to reports that American sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln were struggling with a long deployment, Trump said they hadn’t been deployed “nearly long enough.” And the collapse of trade talks with Canada on Friday threaten Republican prospects in border states including Michigan and Ohio. Each of these cases represents a growing gap between Trump and his base, but none is as ironic as Trump’s stance on data centers. The AI facilities store terabytes of data, but the president can’t get access to the information about them that he needs. Related: The bubble-wrapped president Trump’s 2024 soft launch ( From 2022 ) Here are four new stories from The Atlantic : Sari Horwitz on the gun lobby’s most cynical move yet A reverse Ellis Island What a bicentennial baby knows David Frum on how to lose a trade war Today’s News The Supreme Court allowed the Trump administration to move forward for now with plans to restrict mail-in voting , including directing the Postal Service to help determine which voters receive mail ballots. The ruling is preliminary and allows implementation to proceed while a lower court considers the legality of President Trump’s executive order. Trump said that the United States will impose 50 percent tariffs on Canadian cars, trucks, auto parts, and steel beginning January 1, 2027. The announcement followed Canada’s decision to impose retaliatory tariffs on U.S. products after U.S.-Canada trade talks ended without an agreement over the weekend. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced an “economic D-Day” for Iran, stating that the U.S. will impose new sanctions on more than 60 entities, individuals, and vessels tied to Iran’s nuclear and missile programs; additional sanctions are planned in the coming weeks. Evening Read From left: The comedians Anthony Atamanuik, Sarah Cooper, Alec Baldwin, and Brent Terhune Illustration by The Atlantic. Sources: Theo Wargo / Getty; Dimitrios Kambouris / Getty; @brentterhune / Instagram. The Trump Comedians Are Tired By Will Gottsegen In 2017, as Donald Trump was getting used to the White House furniture, Alec Baldwin was feeling exultant. His impersonation of the new president on Saturday Night Live had made him momentarily inescapable and given the comedy show its highest ratings in years. To capitalize on the momentum, Baldwin co-authored a book-length satirical memoir written from Trump’s perspective. Baldwin’s autobiography—which also came out that year and was excerpted as a cover story for Vanity Fair —noted that his take on the president “seemed to delight nearly everyone in the People’s Republic of Manhattan.” When he accepted an Emmy for his performance in the fall, he addressed Trump directly: “At long last, Mr. President, here is your Emmy.” It was disorienting, then, to hear Baldwin declare, when I spoke with him earlier this summer, that this sort of comedy has become stale, boring, and useless. “None of it’s funny. I don’t find it funny anymore,” he told me. “There’s nothing left to say about Trump.” Read the full article. items.title: Supreme Court upholds Trump bid to curb mail-in ballots for now
items.description: The US Supreme Court gave President Donald Trump a temporary victory on Monday, lifting a lower court block on his executive order curbing the use of mail-in ballots. The Republican president signed an order in March seeking to restrict mail-in voting ahead of the November midterm elections but it was immediately met with multiple legal challenges. Democratic-led states sued the administration on grounds that under the US Constitution, states — and not the federal government — retain broad control over the administration of elections. A district court in Massachusetts blocked implementation of the executive order but the Supreme Court on Monday lifted the judge’s stay, allowing parts of Trump’s directive to go ahead for now. “The District Court lacked jurisdiction to bar the Government from trying to implement” the executive order, the Supreme Court majority said in an unsigned opinion. But the justices withheld final judgment on the merits of the case pending further litigation. “The Court’s disposition of this application does not mean that any measure taken by the Government to implement the Order will necessarily be lawful,” they said. “On that score, time will tell.” The three liberal justices on the nine-member Supreme Court dissented. Trump’s March executive order would require the compilation of lists of eligible voters and for the US Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters who are on the lists. Trump has been a longtime critic of mail-in ballots but has frequently used them himself, including this month when he voted by mail in Florida’s Republican primary. Trump has for years claimed without evidence that mail-in voting is highly vulnerable to fraud, repeatedly linking it to his false assertion that the 2020 presidential election was stolen from him by Democrat Joe Biden. “Mail-in ballots are inherently corrupt,” he said during a July speech on election security. Polls show that Trump’s Republican Party faces a serious threat of losing its narrow control of Congress in the midterm elections in November, particularly in the House of Representatives, the lower chamber. If Democrats win, they have signaled they will block Trump’s agenda and could move to impeach him for the third time. items.title: Coopération Mali-Algérie: le Premier ministre Abdoulaye Maïga porteur d’un message du Président Goïta à son homologue Tebboune
items.description: COOPERATION-MALI-ALGÉRIE-VISITE-PREMIER-MINISTRE Coopération Mali-Algérie: le Premier ministre Abdoulaye Maïga porteur d’un message du Président Goïta à son homologue Tebboune Ouagadougou, 24 août 2026 (AIB)- Le Président algérien, Abdelmadjid Tebboune, a reçu en audience, lundi à Alger, le Premier ministre malien, le Général de division Abdoulaye Maïga, porteur d’un message du Président de la Transition du Mali, le Général d’armée Assimi Goïta, à son homologue algérien. À l’issue de l’audience, le chef du gouvernement malien a réaffirmé la volonté des deux pays de renforcer leur coopération, estimant que « le Mali et l’Algérie sont condamnés à cheminer ensemble, condamnés à œuvrer dans le sens de la prospérité pour les deux peuples ». Cette audience s’inscrit dans le cadre de la visite de travail du Premier ministre malien en Algérie. Plus tôt dans la journée, le Général de division Abdoulaye Maïga s’était recueilli au Monument des Martyrs à Alger. Agence d’information du Burkina

items.title: Colombia faces years of rebuilding after earthquake devastation
items.description: Two weeks after a magnitude 7.4 earthquake devastated western Colombia, the emergency response is giving way to the long-term work of reconstruction. items.title: Guinée : le président Mamadi Doumbouya autorisé à légiférer par ordonnance (décret) ​
items.description: Ce lundi 24 août 2026, le Président de la République, Mamadi Doumbouya, a officiellement promulgué la loi organique L/2026/03/AN, un texte qui l'habilite désormais à légiférer par voie d’ordonnance. ​ Cette décision intervient à la suite de l’avis n°24 rendu le 20 août 2026 par la Cour suprême, confirmant la régularité de la procédure. Avec la signature du décret présidentiel, cette loi organique est dorénavant pleinement exécutoire. ​En pratique, cette habilitation offre au chef de l’État la prérogative d’adopter des règles relevant du domaine de la loi par le biais d'ordonnances, dans le respect rigoureux des conditions et des domaines fixés par l’Assemblée nationale lors de son vote. ​ Aux termes du décret signé, l'acte prend effet immédiatement dès sa date de signature. Il a également été ordonné son enregistrement et sa publication au Journal officiel de la République.

items.title: Aïd Al Mawlid Annabawi : Grâce Royale au profit de 634 personnes
items.description: A l'occasion de l’Aïd Al Mawlid Annabawi, le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu L'assiste, a bien voulu accorder Sa grâce à 634 personnes dont certaines sont en détention et d’autres en liberté, condamnées par différents tribunaux du Royaume, annonce le ministère de la Justice dans un communiqué. En voici le texte : « A l’occasion de l’Aïd Al Mawlid Annabawi de cette année 1448H – 2026G, Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, que Dieu perpétue Sa gloire, a bien voulu accorder Sa grâce à un ensemble de personnes condamnées par différents tribunaux du Royaume. Ces personnes sont au nombre de 619 et se présentent comme suit: * Les bénéficiaires de la Grâce Royale qui sont en détention sont au nombre de 462 détenus se répartissant comme suit: -Grâce sur le reliquat de la peine d’emprisonnement ou de réclusion au profit de 13 détenus. -Remise de la peine d’emprisonnement ou de réclusion au profit de 449 détenus. * Les bénéficiaires de la Grâce Royale qui sont en liberté sont au nombre de 157 personnes se répartissant comme suit : -Grâce sur la peine d’emprisonnement ou son reliquat au profit de 28 personnes. -Grâce sur la peine d’emprisonnement avec maintien de l’amende au profit de 13 personnes. -Grâce sur la peine d’amende au profit de 112 personnes. -Grâce sur la peine d’emprisonnement et d’amende au profit de 04 personnes. En cette glorieuse occasion, Sa Majesté le Roi, que Dieu Le préserve, a bien voulu accorder Sa Grâce à des détenus condamnés dans des affaires d’extrémisme et de terrorisme, qui ont obtenu l’Approbation Royale après avoir officiellement exprimé leur attachement aux constantes et aux sacralités de la Nation et aux institutions nationales, révisé leurs orientations idéologiques et rejeté l’extrémisme et le terrorisme. Ils sont au nombre de 15 personnes, se répartissant comme suit: -Grâce sur le reliquat de la peine privative au profit de 09 détenus. -Remise de la peine privative au profit de 06 détenus. Puisse Dieu garder Sa Majesté le Roi, source de clémence et de miséricorde, perpétuer Sa gloire et préserver Son Altesse Royale le Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan, ainsi que tous les membres de la Famille Royale ». The post Aïd Al Mawlid Annabawi : Grâce Royale au profit de 634 personnes appeared first on Hespress Français - Actualités du Maroc .

items.title: Rabat : Le Roi préside une veillée religieuse en commémoration de l’Aïd Al-Mawlid Annabaoui Acharif
items.description: e Roi Mohammed VI, Amir Al-Mouminine, accompagné du Prince Héritier Moulay El Hassan, du Prince Moulay Rachid et du Prince Moulay Ahmed, a présidé, lundi 11 Rabie-Ier 1448 de l’Hégire, correspondant au 24 août 2026, au Palais Royal à Rabat, une veillée religieuse en commémoration de l’Aïd Al-Mawlid Annabaoui Acharif. Cette veillée religieuse a été marquée par la déclamation de versets du Saint Coran et de panégyriques du Prophète Sidna Mohammed, Prière et Bénédiction sur Lui. A cette occasion, le ministre des Habous et des Affaires islamiques, Ahmed Toufiq, a prononcé devant Sa Majesté le Roi une allocution dans laquelle il a présenté le bilan des activités du Conseil supérieur et des Conseils locaux des Oulémas. Dans son allocution, le ministre a indiqué que le Roi, Amir Al Mouminine, avait, à l'occasion de la célébration de l’Aid Al Mawlid Annabaoui de l'année dernière, bien voulu charger le Conseil Supérieur des Oulémas d'entreprendre de multiples actions pour commémorer l’anniversaire du quinzième siècle de la naissance du Prophète, que la prière et la paix soient sur Lui. Toufiq a souligné, dans ce cadre, que tout au long de l’année, il a été procédé, conformément aux Hautes Orientations du Roi, à la tenue de grandes assemblées où ont été élevées des prières en hommage au Prophète et prêchées les hautes moralités du Sceau des Messagers. Le ministre a affirmé que l’indéfectible attachement manifesté par la Nation marocaine au Prophète s’illustre à travers deux expressions au fondement religieux, l’une d’ordre politique et l’autre à portée émotionnelle. L’expression d’ordre politique, a-t-il expliqué, réside dans la perpétuation de l’héritage de la Commanderie des Croyants, dont sont dépositaires les descendants du Prophète, alors que celle à portée émotionnelle se traduit par la mise en avant par les Marocains des nobles vertus du Messager de Dieu, à travers les livres des deux savants marocains originaires de la ville de Sebta, à savoir Cadi Ayad (« Traité sur les vertus curatives de la connaissance des droits du Prophète ») et Abou Abbès Al Ozfi (« Anthologie de poèmes composés en célébration de la naissance de l’Illustre prophète »), outre l’ouvrage de l’Imam Jazouli « Les guides vers les voies du Bien », dont les Marocains ont su brandir les prières qu’il contenait dans leur lutte sacrée pour libérer les villes occupées situées le long de l’océan atlantique au début de l’ère contemporaine. Et le ministre de poursuivre que la Nation marocaine, qui a cherché naturellement refuge dans la guidance du Prophète par l'obéissance comme témoignage de l’amour voué au Sceau des Messagers, atteste aujourd'hui que ses oulémas et savants, profondément conscients de la quintessence des paroles du Prophète Sidna Mohammed, paix et bénédictions soient sur Lui, œuvrent, dans le cadre du plan de communication « Tassdid Tabligh » à convaincre les gens, avec la plus grande clarté et simplicité, que le monothéisme sur lequel reposent le Saint Coran et la mission du Prophète, s'illustre par la libération morale de l'égoïsme aussi bien individuel que collectif, une libération qui favorise une réforme concrète de la religiosité. Le ministre des Habous et des Affaires islamiques a, ensuite, remis au Souverain l’ouvrage en arabe « Dakhirat Al Muhtaj Fi Assalati Ala Sahibi Alliwae Wa Taj », édité par le ministère des Habous et des Affaires islamiques, en se référant à des dizaines de manuscrits conservés dans des bibliothèques royales, publiques et privées, au Maroc et à l'étranger. Cette publication fait suite aux Hautes Orientations du Roi, que Dieu Le préserve, qui avait appelé, l'année dernière, dans une Lettre adressée au Conseil supérieur des Oulémas, à la commémoration du 15e siècle de la naissance du Prophète Sidna Mohammed, que la Prière et la Paix soient sur Lui, notamment à travers la publication de livres et ouvrages du patrimoine marocain, relatifs aux prières sur le Prophète et aux œuvres des oulémas et savants marocains en la matière. Cette veillée religieuse s’est déroulée en présence du Chef du gouvernement, des Présidents des deux Chambres du Parlement, de Conseillers du Roi, des membres du gouvernement, des présidents des Instances Constitutionnelles, des Officiers supérieurs de l’Etat-Major général des Forces Armées Royales, des membres du corps diplomatique islamique accrédités à Rabat, ainsi que de plusieurs oulémas et des personnalités civiles et militaires. La célébration de cette veillée religieuse par le Roi Mohammed VI, Amir Al-Mouminine, s’inscrit dans la tradition observée par Ses Illustres Ancêtres qui ont constamment veillé à commémorer l’anniversaire de la venue au Monde du Messager de la Miséricorde, le Prophète Sidna Mohammed, que la Prière et la Paix soient sur Lui. Un anniversaire qui marque l’éclosion des lumières de la guidance pour l’Humanité, grâce au message porté par le Sceau des Prophètes, pour répandre les hautes vertus et les valeurs de justice et recommander les bonnes actions pour que l’ensemble des humains vivent dans la paix et l’entente. items.title: Logging in Was Never Supposed to Be This Complicated
items.description: One afternoon earlier this month, I pulled up to the rec center and realized that I had a problem. It was not the three boisterous tweens in the back seat who were clamoring to be set loose in the basketball gym. It was my parking app. I had somehow gotten logged out of Passport Parking, which has become the only way to pay for a spot in much of my town, and it was demanding a four-digit PIN to let me back in. My first guess drew a warning message in red letters: “Invalid PIN. PIN cannot contain 4 sequential numbers, 2 repeated digits, or the last 4 digits of your phone number.” I searched my trusty password manager, which was supposed to spare me these predicaments, but it came up empty. By that point, the kids had run ahead and piled themselves against the gym door, waiting for me to let them in. Lately, the process of accessing apps and websites has grown dizzying. “I’m in password hell,” a colleague confided to me recently. “Every login attempt is playing the lottery.” The problem is not just the sheer number of digital accounts, all of which require their own password, ideally unique and unguessable (which usually also means un-memorizable). It’s the pileup of solutions to that problem: all of the different layers of software offering to remember your passwords, the six-digit codes sent to your phone, the authenticator apps, the passkeys. Browsers and operating systems compete with third-party password managers to generate, store, and autofill your credentials. Most of my logins live in 1Password, but others are stored in Apple’s Passwords app (usually by accident), and still others were created via “single sign-on” features such as those offered by Google and Facebook. I vaguely recall certain apps—Facebook is one—prompting me many years ago to copy down a set of “login recovery codes” that would become extremely important should I ever get locked out of my account. Whatever device I stored them on was probably wiped and sold long ago. Logins have always been a hassle. In the 1990s, forgetting your password sometimes meant mailing a po stcard to your service provider and waiting a week or two for it to mail you a new password. In the early 2010s, hackers learned to steal massive troves of logins and then reuse them on other services to steal people’s identities. Things spiraled from there; services started requiring unique, complex passwords with arbitrary requirements. These days, the user experience of logging in is “probably worse than ever,” Troy Hunt, a cybersecurity expert who runs the website Have I Been Pwned, told me. “There’s just no consistency.” Password managers promised a way out, but they often don’t work as seamlessly as you might hope. I click to autofill my password somewhere, and a 1Password authorization appears, only for an iCloud Keychain authorization to pop up directly over it, preventing me from clicking on the 1Password one. When I manually enter a login I thought I remembered, my browser prompts me to remember it; only after I hit “Save” (pro tip: Do not do this) does the website inform me that the password was not recognized. Even when you log in successfully, there’s the tedious dance of waiting for a six-digit authorization code to appear on your phone or in your email, which defeats the concept of a single password for everything. And if you’re somewhere without cell service or you’re sharing a login with someone who isn’t around, you might just be out of luck. All of these steps serve a purpose. At least in theory, each added layer helps prevent hacks and breaches. Erring on the side of safety is worth an amount of inconvenience. At the same time, extra steps can introduce security problems of their own. Last year, Hunt fell for a clever phishing scheme when he clicked a link to log in to his newsletter service. His password manager failed to autofill his information, which should have alerted him that something was wrong, he said. But like the rest of us, he was so used to things not working that he went ahead and manually entered his credentials on a site that turned out to be an impostor, designed to steal and exploit them. None of these obstacles is insurmountable on its own. My problem with Apple’s native password manager fighting with 1Password, for instance, was eventually solved with a 10-minute foray into the bowels of my device settings. But together, they amount to a near-daily irritant. For the less tech-savvy, the situation can be overwhelming. My recent attempts to help my mother fix her password-storage system—which involved loose-leaf notepad sheets full of hand-scrawled credentials scattered around her house like Easter eggs—consumed the better part of a day. By the end, she had all of her credentials updated, validated, and stored in a password manager, just as the experts have been advising for years. But even then, her preferred browser, Google Chrome, showed no interest in surfacing the credentials we had stashed in Apple’s Keychain. And some websites short-circuited her attempts to log in by prompting her to set up a “passkey,” which she interpreted as meaning that her password had failed and she needed to scrap it and set up a new one. Cybersecurity experts will tell you that passkeys—which typically entail logging in to apps or websites with a face or fingerprint scan instead of a password—are the future. When they work properly, they’re both painless and secure. “It may get to a point where we’re all using passkeys and we don’t even know we’re using passkeys,” Lorrie Cranor, a computer-science professor at Carnegie Mellon University who researches privacy and cybersecurity, told me. “I just say ‘Log in’ and I smile at it, and it gets my passkey, and I’m logged in.” But that future isn’t here yet, and in the present, passkeys have added a new layer of frustration. Part of the problem is that virtually no one seems to know what they are. “The fact that even I have trouble explaining them should be a clue,” Cranor said. Her past research on the rollout of two-factor authentication suggests that most people tend to resist new security features for as long as they can. Companies can nudge them, but for websites and apps trying to attract and retain users, pushing people to adopt an unfamiliar authentication technology risks scaring them away. To further complicate matters, passkeys generally aren’t yet replacing passwords altogether, even on sites that use them. Because many passkeys live on your device, one that works on your phone might not work on your laptop, and one that works on your personal laptop might not work on your office device. So you still need a password that works across devices as a backup. It’s a lot, Dave Lewis, 1Password’s global-security adviser, acknowledged to me in an email. “The problem is cognitive overload,” he said. “All these tools are trying to help, but they don’t always work together intuitively.” Still, he disagreed that the situation has never been worse: “When the alternative was using the same password across dozens of accounts or putting it on a sticky note, the fact that people now have password managers, passkeys, biometrics, and multifactor authentication is a good thing.” The mess might compound before it improves. Hacking attempts have been multiplying as crooks harness AI tools. Companies are adding even more security layers that make logging in harder, and they are pleading for people to make the switch to passkeys. On the bright side, maybe the seamless biometric future is actually within sight, and all of our login woes will soon be over. Then again, that’s what we were promised with password managers too.

items.title: Tarifs péage autoroute Dakar-Kaolack : la Société nationale autoroutes du Sénégal dément les rumeurs sur les réseaux sociaux
items.description: La Société nationale autoroutes du Sénégal (SN ADS SA) dément les rumeurs véhiculées sur les réseaux sociaux faisant état d'un tarif aller-retour de 15 000 FCFA pour le péage de l'autoroute Dakar-Kaolack. Les précisions ont été faites à travers une note publiée lundi. La Société nationale autoroutes du Sénégal (SN ADS SA) apporte un démenti catégorique aux informations erronées diffusées récemment sur les réseaux sociaux, faisant état d'un tarif aller-retour de 15 000 FCFA pour le péage de l'autoroute Dakar-Kaolack. « La SN ADS SA tient à rétablir la vérité des faits auprès des usagers de la route et de l'opinion publique : le tarif appliqué pour un véhicule particulier sur le trajet Dakar-Kaolack est de 6 500 FCFA sur un parcours de 184 km, soit 35 FCFA par kilomètre », indique le texte de la SN ADS SA. Concernant le nouveau tronçon Mbour-Kaolack nouvellement ouvert à la circulation, la même source informe que le tarif pour la même catégorie de véhicule est de 3 000 FCFA sur 100 km, soit 30 FCFA par kilomètre. A lire aussi : Autoroute Mbour–Fatick–Kaolack : ouverture définitive à la circulation ce samedi « Les redevances du péage actuellement appliquées répondent à une logique de tarifs sociaux, étudiés pour garantir l'accessibilité au plus grand nombre. La SN ADS SA invite le grand public à ne pas relayer ces rumeurs infondées et à se référer exclusivement aux canaux d'information officiels de la société », conclut la note. Mariama DIEME

items.title: Mercato : la pépite guinéenne Ousmane Diabaté signe à Newcastle United
items.description: Ce lundi 24 août 2026, le jeune milieu de terrain guinéen Ousmane Diabaté s'est officiellement engagé avec le club anglais de Newcastle United pour une durée de quatre ans, assortie d'une année supplémentaire en option, a-t-on appris de source officielle. Bien qu'aucun chiffre officiel n'ait été divulgué, des medias turs indiquent que, le montant total du transfert s'élèverait à 3,1millions d'euros, dont 1,1 millions de bonus inclus. Cette signature marque l'aboutissement de l'ascension fulgurante du natif de N’Zérékoré. Transféré de la SOAR Academy vers le club turque de Gençlerbirliği SK il y a moins d’un an, Diabaté s'est rapidement imposé grâce à sa rigueur, son professionnalisme et sa grande capacité d’adaptation. Ses performances remarquées en Turquie lui ouvrent désormais les portes de la Premier League. Afin de finaliser les démarches administratives et de cumuler le nombre de matchs requis pour l'obtention de son permis de travail en Angleterre, le joueur restera en prêt à Gençlerbirliği durant la première partie de saison. Son intégration définitive au sein de l'effectif des Magpies est prévue au plus tard lors du prochain mercato hivernal.
